sections.text_helper: Section 24.4.12 "Timer-controlled operation" in chapter 24 (Operational amplifier (OPAMP)), RM0522 Rev 1, page 739.
sections.section_content:
Certain timer channels (see Table183) can toggle the control of the operational amplifier
multiplexers between the primary configuration defined through the OPAMP_CSR register
and the secondary configuration defined through the OPAMP_TCMR register.
Once configured, the mechanism operates even when the OPAMP clock is disabled.
As an example, this can be used for dual motor control. Figure164 illustrates the use of a
timer compare output toggling the OPAMP primary (default) and secondary configurations,
to measure alternatively the currents of the three phases of a motor, then of the other motor.
[Figure 164. Timer-controlled operation for a dual motor application]
Timer-controlled input selection
This operation is activated by writing a value other than 0 to the TIMCM_SEL[2:0] bitfield of
the OPAMP_TCMR register, thus selecting one of the opamp_tcX signals. As long as the
selected signal is low, the input selectors are controlled with the VP_SEL[1:0] and
VM_SEL[1:0] bitfields of the OPAMP_CSR register. As long as it is high, the input selectors
are controlled with the VPS_SEL[1:0] and VMS_SEL bitfields of the OPAMP_TCMR
register. Writing 0 to TIMCM_SEL[2:0] (default upon reset) makes the input selectors
steadily controlled with VP_SEL[1:0] and VM_SEL[1:0].
Table183 gives the correspondence between the opamp_tcX and the timer signals.
[Table 183. Timer-controlled input selection]
Timer-controlled programmable gain and PGA flavor
This operation is activated by writing a value other than 0 to the TIMPGA_SEL[2:0] bitfield of
the OPAMP_TCMR register, thus selecting one of opamp_tpX signals. As long as the
selected signal is low, the programmable gain and PGA flavor selectors are controlled with
the PGA_GAIN[4:0] bitfield of the OPAMP_CSR register. As long as it is high, the input
selectors are controlled with the PGAS_GAIN[4:0] bitfield of the OPAMP_TCMR register.
Writing 0 to TIMPGA_SEL[2:0] (default upon reset) makes the programmable gain and PGA
flavor selectors steadily controlled with PGA_GAIN[4:0].
The following table gives the correspondence of the opamp_tpX signals to timer signals.
[Table 184. Timer-controlled programmable gain selection]
